input_query: Can you explain how photosynthesis works?

input_evidence_items.content: Photosynthesis uses sunlight, water, and CO2 to produce glucose and oxygen
The process occurs in chloroplasts which contain chlorophyll
The light-dependent reactions produce ATP and NADPH

description: Mitosis vs meiosis comparison with evidence

input_evidence_items.content: Mitosis produces two identical diploid daughter cells
Meiosis produces four genetically different haploid gametes
Mitosis is for growth and repair, meiosis is for sexual reproduction

input_query: Why does the heart need valves?

input_evidence_items.content: Heart valves prevent backflow of blood between chambers
The heart has four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic

description: Cell transport clarification for struggling student
input_query: I don't get the difference between diffusion and osmosis

input_evidence_items.content: Diffusion is the movement of molecules from high to low concentration
Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a semipermeable membrane

input_query: How does HIV attack the immune system?

input_evidence_items.content: HIV specifically targets and destroys CD4+ T-helper cells
Without T-helper cells, the immune system cannot coordinate responses to infections
HIV is transmitted through bodily fluids including blood and semen

description: Genetics punnet square, simplified for grade 8
input_query: How do I use a Punnett square?

input_evidence_items.content: A Punnett square shows possible genotypes of offspring from two parents
Each parent contributes one allele for each gene to their offspring
Dominant alleles mask recessive alleles in heterozygous pairs

description: Personalized explanation for weak student on food webs
input_query: Can you explain trophic levels again? I got them wrong on the quiz.

input_evidence_items.content: Trophic levels describe an organism's position in a food chain
Producers (plants) are at trophic level 1, primary consumers at level 2
Energy decreases by about 90% at each trophic level

description: Ethiopian endemic species with Amharic result expected
input_query: Tell me about Ethiopian wolves in the Bale Mountains

input_evidence_items.content: The Ethiopian wolf is a critically endangered canid found only in Ethiopia
Bale Mountains National Park is the primary habitat for Ethiopian wolves
Ethiopian wolves primarily feed on giant mole rats and other small mammals

input_query: Walk me through the nitrogen cycle

input_evidence_items.content: Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric N2 to ammonia by bacteria
Nitrification converts ammonia to nitrites then nitrates for plant use
Denitrification returns nitrogen gas to the atmosphere completing the cycle

input_query: How are arteries different from veins?

input_evidence_items.content: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure
Veins carry blood toward the heart under low pressure with valves
Arteries have thick muscular walls, veins have thinner walls

input_query: Explain natural selection using animals I know from Ethiopia

input_evidence_items.content: Natural selection favors organisms better adapted to their environment
The Ethiopian wolf adapted to high-altitude habitats in the Bale Mountains
Gelada baboons developed social structures adapted to Ethiopian highland grasslands
Flowers contain male stamens and female pistils for reproduction
Pollination transfers pollen from stamen to pistil for fertilization
After fertilization, ovules develop into seeds and the ovary becomes fruit

description: Immune system overview with vaccination context

input_evidence_items.content: Vaccines expose the immune system to harmless antigens to build immunity
Memory B cells remember the antigen for faster future response
Herd immunity protects vulnerable populations when enough people are vaccinated

description: DNA replication explanation for advanced student
input_query: Explain the process of DNA replication in detail

input_evidence_items.content: DNA replication occurs during the S phase of the cell cycle
DNA helicase unwinds the double helix by breaking hydrogen bonds
DNA polymerase adds complementary nucleotides to each template strand

input_query: How does the endocrine system control body functions?

input_evidence_items.content: The endocrine system uses hormones as chemical messengers via the bloodstream
Glands like the pituitary, thyroid, and adrenal produce specific hormones
Hormones bind to target cell receptors to trigger specific responses
